{"documentId": "f_dc45e0e5a8b8635c1b82b2", "title": "Beta message rule", "name": "Beta message rule", "revisionId": "740e0d0bac", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T17:10:54Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T17:10:54Z", "text": "Beta message rule
A message is anything the game puts on a player's phone while the game is closed.
Run these tests in order and stop at the first one that fails.
1. The feature behind it is in the beta.
2. The client can send it without a server.
3. The client already schedules it.
4. It can reach the players it is written for. A player only counts once our own permission ask has happened, the settings toggle doesn't count. It fails only if none of them count.
5. It fires on the right day. The hour doesn't matter for beta, the day does.
6. Vincent has seen it arrive on both iOS and Android.
Go: it passes all six. Drop: it fails test 1, or the client already covers it under another message, then name that message. Hold: anything else, and name the test it failed.
In the beta means live in Zombie Match today or on the BETA list of the ZM ROADMAP board.
Neither status column on the sheet decides anything.
What Vincent counts as seen is in his QA note. The permission ask is Robert's call.
The final headline is the latest line I've called. A line that differs from what the client ships needs a string ticket under DES-314, because the strings are hard-coded, so open one when you make the call. Emoji don't count as a different line. Final headline and String change are only for Go rows. Audience is who the ask says it's for.
Drop tickets go to Canceled, Go tickets stay as they are, Hold tickets go back to Todo unless the roadmap says otherwise.
"}

## 🧩 **Endless Mode – Engineering Summary**

### 🔧 Initial Setup

- Game starts with **40–45 sets** (a set = 3 items).
- **8 unique item types**, with size distribution:
  - 2 Large, 4 medium, 2 Small.
- Entire **item pool is defined by the designer** for each endless variant.
- Monsters also follow **30-second "tracks"**, authored by designers using level editor tools.

---

### 🔄 Refill System (Every 30 seconds)

1. **Track matched items** from the last 30 seconds.
2. **Refill those exact items** to keep total set count at 40–45.
3. Each refill is simulated and checked against a **growing Unique Item Cap**:

Refill #Time (s)Unique Cap130826093909412010.........1236014

---

### 🧠 Refill Logic Rules

1. **Simulate a refill**: Replace all matched items 1:1.
2. **Count unique items** on the new board.
3. If unique count is **below cap**:
   - Attempt to **substitute refilled items** with new unique items one-by-one.
   - After each substitution, re-check unique count.
4. If still short:
   - Remove a **fraction of total sets** = `#missingUniques / targetUniqueCap`.
   - Replace them with random sets using new unique items to reach the cap.

**Key principle:** Total number of sets never changes; only uniqueness does.

---

- **Builds power** by matching items:
  `NukePower += itemAttackPower × 10% × comboMultiplier`
- **Combo System**:
  - Starts at **1x**.
  - Combo meter fills after each match and **decays** over time.
  - If matched before timeout, combo increases.
  - Decay window shrinks by 0.25s each level (starts at 4.5s).
  - Max achievable combo: 18x.
  - The **next match** receives the combo multiplier shown.

content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_933e2d4147dc0fecd537aa\", \"title\": \"ZM QA Checklist.docx\", \"name\": \"ZM QA Checklist.docx\", \"revisionId\": \"d23fb3d30a\", \"createdTime\": \"2025-06-02T19:53:59Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2025-06-02T19:58:36Z\", \"text\": \"1. Smoke Test Checklist (Basic Functionality)\\nCore Gameplay\\nMatch 3 identical objects triggers correct animation and throws to zombies\\nKilling all regular zombies completes the level\\nKilling boss zombie completes the level, even if regular zombies remain\\nMismatched objects do not trigger any zombie damage\\nMatching fewer than 3 does not trigger zombie damage\\nLevel starts and ends properly without crashing\\nNo soft-locks when all matchable objects are exhausted\\nDifferent object types trigger distinct visual/audio feedback\\nBoss hit and kill animations play correctly\\nBoosts and Power-Ups\\nBoost button is tappable and triggers intended effect\\nFast-match bonus throws items more quickly\\nBoss-targeting item exclusively damages boss\\nUsing multiple boosts doesn't crash or bug the system\\nBoost usage shows visual feedback and is consumed properly\\nUI / UX\\nObject tap, drag, and drop interactions are responsive\\nPause, resume, restart functions operate correctly\\nHealth bars for zombies and bosses update correctly\\nEnd-of-level UI appears consistently (success/failure)\\nHUD reflects real-time status of lives, moves, boosts\\nLevel Flow\\nLevel begins from map screen correctly\\nLevel completion popup appears\\nLevel failure conditions trigger properly (moves/time out)\\nRetry, next level, and home buttons work as expected\\nGame state saved between sessions (e.g. retry level works)\\nPacks & Upgrades\\nPack opening animation and item rewards are displayed\\nObject inventory updates correctly after pack opens\\nUpgrade button is clickable only when enough materials exist\\nUpgrade improves stats (visible in UI and functional in play)\\nDuplicate objects are merged or stacked correctly in inventory\\n---\\n2. Edge Case Testing\\nGameplay Edge Cases\\nMatching 3 items when only 1 zombie remains (overkill behavior)\\nUsing a boss-target item when no boss is present\\nMatching more than 3 identical objects (combo or error handling)\\nAttempting invalid match (e.g., rapid-tap glitch abuse)\\nBoost used in final second of level - is effect honored?\\nLevel ends while object is mid-air - does game finalize properly?\\nProgression and Upgrades\\nOpening a pack with max inventory space - is overflow handled?\\nUpgrading an already-maxed object - proper error or feedback\\nInternet lost during pack opening - graceful recovery?\\nPlayer skips tutorial - is core gameplay still understandable?\\nMonetization\\nPurchase attempt without internet connection\\nCanceling mid-purchase - no item rewarded\\nBuying the same pack twice in a row - no duplication bugs\\nReceiving bonus pack from event, but pack cap reached\\nPurchase UI feedback is consistent across currencies (soft/hard)\\nCross-platform purchase support (if applicable)\\nUI/UX Edge Cases\\nSwitching apps mid-level and returning - game state intact\\nRotating screen (if supported) - UI remains consistent\\nSpamming object taps or boosts - system remains stable\\nMemory usage with long sessions or dozens of objects on screen\\nLanguage change mid-session - UI responds correctly\\n---\\n3. Persona-Based Scenario Testing\\nCasual Player (Slow Progression, No Spending)\\nCan complete early levels without boosts or upgrades\\nGets regular pack rewards from natural progression\\nLives deplete on failure; soft-fail feedback encourages retry\\nLevel difficulty gradually increases but remains fair\\nOnboarding tutorial teaches all core mechanics clearly\\nAds appear after failure or level end but don't overwhelm\\nStrategic Player (High Skill, Selective Spending)\\nCan clear levels through object prioritization and combos\\nFinds value in boss-targeting and fast-match mechanics\\nUpgrades objects from earned packs efficiently\\nChallenge levels or boss levels provide skill-based tests\\nProgression unlocks strategic layers like enemy types, object effects\\nPayer / Whale (Frequent Buyer)\\nCan immediately purchase packs, boosts, lives\\nProgresses faster and accesses higher-level content\\nBoost stacking and usage remains balanced and not overpowered\\nUI confirms all transactions and feedback is instant\\nExclusive content available but doesn't break balance\\nGrinder (Long Play Sessions)\\nMultiple sessions without restart work smoothly\\nGame performance holds after 10+ levels without lag\\nNo daily limits block grinding, but progression remains balanced\\nPerformance degrades gracefully on low-end devices\\nInventory and stats remain stable across extended gameplay\\nEvent-Driven Player\\nEvent banners load and link properly\\nEvent rewards contribute meaningfully to progress\\nSpecial event levels integrate with base mechanics\\nTimed events expire gracefully and give appropriate fallback content\\nLimited-time offers and countdowns are clear and functional\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_933e2d4147dc0fecd537aa", "title": "ZM QA Checklist.docx", "name": "ZM QA Checklist.docx", "revisionId": "d23fb3d30a", "createdTime": "2025-06-02T19:53:59Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-06-02T19:58:36Z", "text": "1. Smoke Test Checklist (Basic Functionality)
Core Gameplay
Match 3 identical objects triggers correct animation and throws to zombies
Killing all regular zombies completes the level
Killing boss zombie completes the level, even if regular zombies remain
Mismatched objects do not trigger any zombie damage
Matching fewer than 3 does not trigger zombie damage
Level starts and ends properly without crashing
No soft-locks when all matchable objects are exhausted
Different object types trigger distinct visual/audio feedback
Boss hit and kill animations play correctly
Boosts and Power-Ups
Boost button is tappable and triggers intended effect
Fast-match bonus throws items more quickly
Boss-targeting item exclusively damages boss
Using multiple boosts doesn't crash or bug the system
Boost usage shows visual feedback and is consumed properly
UI / UX
Object tap, drag, and drop interactions are responsive
Pause, resume, restart functions operate correctly
Health bars for zombies and bosses update correctly
End-of-level UI appears consistently (success/failure)
HUD reflects real-time status of lives, moves, boosts
Level Flow
Level begins from map screen correctly
Level completion popup appears
Level failure conditions trigger properly (moves/time out)
Retry, next level, and home buttons work as expected
Game state saved between sessions (e.g. retry level works)
Packs & Upgrades
Pack opening animation and item rewards are displayed
Object inventory updates correctly after pack opens
Upgrade button is clickable only when enough materials exist
Upgrade improves stats (visible in UI and functional in play)
Duplicate objects are merged or stacked correctly in inventory
---
2. Edge Case Testing
Gameplay Edge Cases
Matching 3 items when only 1 zombie remains (overkill behavior)
Using a boss-target item when no boss is present
Matching more than 3 identical objects (combo or error handling)
Attempting invalid match (e.g., rapid-tap glitch abuse)
Boost used in final second of level - is effect honored?
Level ends while object is mid-air - does game finalize properly?
Progression and Upgrades
Opening a pack with max inventory space - is overflow handled?
Upgrading an already-maxed object - proper error or feedback
Internet lost during pack opening - graceful recovery?
Player skips tutorial - is core gameplay still understandable?
Monetization
Purchase attempt without internet connection
Canceling mid-purchase - no item rewarded
Buying the same pack twice in a row - no duplication bugs
Receiving bonus pack from event, but pack cap reached
Purchase UI feedback is consistent across currencies (soft/hard)
Cross-platform purchase support (if applicable)
UI/UX Edge Cases
Switching apps mid-level and returning - game state intact
Rotating screen (if supported) - UI remains consistent
Spamming object taps or boosts - system remains stable
Memory usage with long sessions or dozens of objects on screen
Language change mid-session - UI responds correctly
---
3. Persona-Based Scenario Testing
Casual Player (Slow Progression, No Spending)
Can complete early levels without boosts or upgrades
Gets regular pack rewards from natural progression
Lives deplete on failure; soft-fail feedback encourages retry
Level difficulty gradually increases but remains fair
Onboarding tutorial teaches all core mechanics clearly
Ads appear after failure or level end but don't overwhelm
Strategic Player (High Skill, Selective Spending)
Can clear levels through object prioritization and combos
Finds value in boss-targeting and fast-match mechanics
Upgrades objects from earned packs efficiently
Challenge levels or boss levels provide skill-based tests
Progression unlocks strategic layers like enemy types, object effects
Payer / Whale (Frequent Buyer)
Can immediately purchase packs, boosts, lives
Progresses faster and accesses higher-level content
Boost stacking and usage remains balanced and not overpowered
UI confirms all transactions and feedback is instant
Exclusive content available but doesn't break balance
Grinder (Long Play Sessions)
Multiple sessions without restart work smoothly
Game performance holds after 10+ levels without lag
No daily limits block grinding, but progression remains balanced
Performance degrades gracefully on low-end devices
Inventory and stats remain stable across extended gameplay
Event-Driven Player
Event banners load and link properly
Event rewards contribute meaningfully to progress
Special event levels integrate with base mechanics
Timed events expire gracefully and give appropriate fallback content
Limited-time offers and countdowns are clear and functional
"}

input.bodyText:
Beta player messages – what we say to players (Oct 1, 2025)

Retention we're judged on: Sep 15 install week (warehouse, USER_COHORT_RETENTION, Zombie Match 3D)
- iOS: 237 installs, D1 31.65%, D7 9.28%
- Android: 103 installs, D1 37.86%, D7 10.68%

Lapsed reminders the client schedules, day by day (NotificationManager, rescheduled every time the app closes, so "day" means days since the last session)
- Day 1: Lapsed 1 day, "The Horde Is Growing… 🧟‍♂️". Go.
- Days 2–6: nothing.
- Day 7: Lapsed 7 days. Go, with the headline changing to "Your Squad Needs You Back" (DES-346). The client still ships "They’ve Taken Over… Can You Stop Them? 😱" until that string lands.
- Days 14, 21, 28: the same Lapsed 7 days message again (weekly batch of 4). This already covers the 14-day ask, so DES-344 is a Drop.
- Day 3 and day 30: not scheduled. Both asks (DES-342, DES-343) are Hold on test 3.
- Nothing after day 28.
Only players who have been through our own permission ask (after level 20) get any of these. The settings toggle doesn't count and neither does the iOS launch popup.

Already scheduled by the client but still a Hold, and why
- Lives recharged (DES-315), test 6: Vincent took his tick off. On iOS 0.3.49 it didn't arrive after a full refill (tried twice).
- Finish first mission (DES-318), test 4: it targets players below level 20, but our permission ask only runs after level 20, so none of them count. It only arrived for Vincent with the settings toggle on.
- Plague Race start (DES-319), test 6: the iOS pass was on the 5-minute-timer build. On the real 0.3.40 it never showed. Android is fine.
- Weekly Leaderboard reset (DES-320), test 5: it fires 7/14/21/28 days after the app last closed, not on the server's weekly reset day.

Totals across all 32 messages (14 sheet rows + 18 asks): 2 Go, 24 Hold, 6 Drop. The Go list is on the Push Notifications card for Vincent. The full per-message sheet is "Beta player messages – calls (Oct 1)" in this folder. Held tickets go to Backlog, unassigned, per the BETA card.

content.text:
I've done everything in Leonard's DM and told him the counts there. Of the 32 messages (14 rows on the PNs Beta tab plus 18 asks), **2 are Go, 24 Hold and 6 Drop**. The sheet said six were Ready; only two pass the message rule doc.

**The calls**
- **Go (2):** Lapsed 1 day and Lapsed 7 days. In a Slack thread on Sep 29, Leonard asked for the Lapsed 7 days headline to become "Your Squad Needs You Back". The game still shows "They've Taken Over… Can You Stop Them?", so I opened DES-346 under DES-314 to change the line in the code.
- **Drop (6):**
  - Hourly Coins, Treasure Hunt, Streak Fever and Axe Arena: none of them are in Zombie Match and none are on the BETA list.
  - Lapsed 14 days: the Lapsed 7 days reminder already goes out again on day 14.
  - Comeback gift: Leonard said on the ticket it's a version 2 idea.
- **Hold (24):** mostly asks the game doesn't schedule yet (test 3) or that need a server send (test 2). Four Holds are reminders the game already schedules, but they still fail a test:
  - Lives recharged: Vincent took his tick off after it didn't arrive on iOS 0.3.49.
  - Finish first mission: it's aimed at players below level 20, but our permission ask only runs after level 20.
  - Plague Race: Vincent's iOS check was on the build with shortened timers, which doesn't count.
  - Weekly Leaderboard reset: it fires 7 days after the player's last session, not on the day the leaderboard resets.

**What's in place**
- **Drive folder:** the sheet ("Beta player messages – calls (Oct 1)", one row per message with your seven columns) and the one-page note. The note starts with the Sep 15 cohort week: iOS D1 31.65% / D7 9.28%, Android D1 37.86% / D7 10.68%.
- **Trello:** the push notifications card has a checklist with the two Go messages for Vincent.
- **Tickets:** each one has its call as a comment. Go tickets stay as they were, and Drops are Canceled. Holds went to Backlog with no assignee, not Todo: the BETA list on the ZM ROADMAP board says held tickets sit there until the beta build is out, and the rule doc defers to the roadmap.
- **No new ticket for Win & Collect:** Calvin's DES-313 already covers that sheet row under a different name, so I used it.
- **Emails:** Calvin, Brian, Robert, Oliver, Julia, Owen and Martin each got one saying what happened to their asks. Leonard didn't, as he asked.

Two calls are my reading of the code rather than something already written down:
- **Weekly Leaderboard reset:** I held it because the game schedules it from the player's last session, not the server's reset date. If you'd count that as firing on the right day, it moves to Hold on test 6 instead. It would still be a Hold, because Vincent's check doesn't cover the reset day.
- **Free shop coins (Martin):** I kept it separate from Hourly Coins because the free shop coins are live and hourly coins aren't.
